# 1 Clement Chapter 23 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 23 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_023_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 23

**23:1** The all-merciful and beneficent Father has compassion on those who fear him, and gently and kindly he bestows his gracious gifts upon those who draw near to him with a simple mind.

**23:2** Therefore let us not be double-minded, neither let our soul harbor false expectations regarding his excellent and glorious gifts.

**23:3** Let this scripture be far from us where it says: "Wretched are the double-minded, those who doubt in their soul and say: 'These things we heard also in the time of our fathers, and behold we have grown old, and none of these things has happened to us.'"

**23:4** O foolish ones! Compare yourselves to a tree: take a vine. First it sheds its leaves, then a shoot comes, then a leaf, then a flower, and after these a sour berry, then a full ripe grape. You see that in a short time the fruit of the tree comes to ripeness.

**23:5** Truly swiftly and suddenly shall his will be accomplished, the scripture also bearing witness to it: "He shall come quickly and not delay; and the Lord shall come suddenly to his temple, even the Holy One, whom you await."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of Codex Alexandrinus with maximal literalness. Double-mindedness (dipsychos) is rendered literally throughout.*
